newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.bank raises benchmark rate, zloty slips.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.bank raises benchmark rate, zloty slips.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland reaffirmed its will to keep market rates growing in the near-term and increased the benchmark 14-day reverse repo rate by 0.42 point to 23.00 percent on Tuesday.
Dealers said, however, that the NBP would probably keep its open market operation rates flat around the 23 percent level in the near-term after rejecting bids for higher rates on Tuesday.
"This level of 23 percent seems to satisfy the NBP for now, but this may change as the situation on the market changes," said Marek Lusztyn, dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

Analysts said the reverse repo rise was another NBP move to curb credit expansion and limit the current account deficit while taking advantage of recent zloty falls which would discourage foreign short-term capital from pouring in.
But they said the NBP may have to push market rates higher, or further increase obligatory reserves for banks, if the 23 percent level does not sufficiently cool credit action.

"Yields on treasury bills could rise further to around 22.20/50 percent...without attracting much interest from foreigners, who have mixed emotions about Poland at the moment," said Maciej Kwiatkowski, dealer at Societe Generale.
The money market continued to be plagued by surplus cash despite Tuesday's 2.8 billion zloty NBP drainage and bill sale.

Overnight rates closed at 2.50/6.50 percent against Monday's 0.50/4.50 as banks tried to place cash on the market after squaring required reserve positions before the monthly account period ends on July 30.

Tommorow/next rates closed around 4.00 percent against Monday's close at 4.36/13.00. The maximum yield of 91-day NBP-bills remained at 23 percent at Tuesday's 942 million zloty sale, but the average yield eased to 22.98 percent.
The zloty closed slightly softer at -1.35/-1.44 percent from the trading band centre against Monday's -1.23/-1.36 after a domestic client order pushed the Polish unit lower.
It closed at 3.4680/90 to the dollar, against 3.4645/95 on Monday and at 1.8895/15 to the mark, against 1.8770/90.
"Today's currency-selling sentiment was restrained by expectations that the NBP would intervene (if the zloty weakened further)," said Jaroslaw Dryjski, a forex dealer at Bank Slaski SA.

Dealers said the zloty could remain pinned to support levels in the near term, amid uncertainty about next year's budget deficit, the September parliamentary elections and a growing current account deficit.
